expectations.text: A PNG deliverable exists with its long side at least 2000 pixels and an alpha channel (RGBA)
The structure is rendered in tube style (continuous backbone trace), not cartoon ribbons/arrowed strands
expectations.evidence: Viewed 6mrr_tube_w2.5_outline.png: continuous rounded tube traces for both chains — smooth tube spirals at the helices, no flat ribbon coils and no strand arrowheads.

expectations.text: If a viewer HTML artifact is present in outputs, its embedded py2dmol config pins style "tube" and width 2.5 (the custom parameters flowed through)
The requested custom look is honored rather than the publication default: strokes visibly heavier than a stock tube render, or the config width value as programmatic evidence
expectations.evidence: Programmatic: viewer HTML pins width=2.5. Visually corroborated: strokes in the PNG are bold heavy bands with the full outline treatment rendered around each trace — visibly heavier than a stock tube render.

notes: The runner had to hand-author spec.json in an editor (viewer: tube, chain color, width 2.5, outline full) because the old skill only accepts styling through a declarative spec, not CLI flags. Output is fully equivalent to the with_skill run (same 2494x2494 RGBA render); the difference is ergonomics, not correctness.
